title: Lambda + SQS production debug runbook
hook: When the pager fires on queue lag, you need an ordered checklist — not random log grepping. This runbook ties SQS metrics, Lambda signals, DLQ, Logs Insights, and X-Ray into a repeatable incident workflow.

blocks.text: A debug runbook is a sequenced investigation: confirm consumer health, check error and throttle metrics, inspect DLQ, query logs for patterns, trace slow requests, validate visibility timeout configuration. Each step has a decision branch — continue or stop with root cause.

blocks.text: Senior on-call engineers are judged by time-to-diagnosis not time-to-random-fix. Scaling Lambda without checking Errors wastes money when code is broken. Visibility misconfiguration looks like consumer failure. A runbook prevents skipping DLQ inspection.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: age → concurrency → errors → DLQ → logs → trace → visibility. Fix root cause before scale. Document in alarm description.

items.body: Compare visibility timeout to Lambda timeout × 6.

diagram.title: Runbook decision tree

snippet.label: Step 1-3 — dashboard metrics one-liner
snippet.code:
QUEUE=orders
FN=payment-processor
for M in ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible; do
  aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/SQS \
    --metric-name $M --dimensions Name=QueueName,Value=$QUEUE \
    --start-time $(date -u -v-30M +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
    --period 60 --statistics Maximum --output table
done
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/Lambda \
  --metric-name ConcurrentExecutions --dimensions Name=FunctionName,Value=$FN \
  --start-time $(date -u -v-30M +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) --end-time $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) \
  --period 60 --statistics Maximum --output table
snippet.explanation: Copy-paste incident starter — run in first 2 minutes of page.

snippet.label: Step 4 — DLQ sample message
snippet.explanation: visibility-timeout 0 for peek without hiding. Check ApproximateReceiveCount attribute.

snippet.label: Step 5 — Logs Insights error query
snippet.code:
aws logs start-query \
  --log-group-name /aws/lambda/payment-processor \
  --start-time $(date -u -v-1H +%s) --end-time $(date -u +%s) \
  --query-string 'fields @timestamp, @message, errorCode, orderId
| filter level = "error" or @message like /Task timed out/
| sort @timestamp desc | limit 50'
snippet.explanation: Structured level field or regex fallback for unstructured legacy logs.

snippet.label: Step 7 — compare visibility vs Lambda timeout
snippet.code:
aws sqs get-queue-attributes \
  --queue-url https://sqs.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/123/orders \
  --attribute-names VisibilityTimeout

aws lambda get-function-configuration \
  --function-name payment-processor \
  --query '{Timeout: Timeout, VpcConfig: VpcConfig}'
snippet.explanation: Visibility should be ≥ 6 × Lambda Timeout. VPC config hints ENI cold start investigation.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Scale concurrency before checking Errors. Ignore DLQ. Skip visibility timeout check. No correlation ID in logs — cannot trace one bad message.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: game-day exercise inject fault — team follows runbook to diagnosis under 15 minutes. CloudWatch dashboard pre-built with all runbook metrics. Automate step 1-3 in incident Slack bot. Post-incident: if step skipped, update runbook.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying 'I would scale Lambda.' Strong answer: ordered triage — metrics prove consumer running, errors ruled out, then scale or fix visibility.

interviewTakeaways: Runbook order: queue age → concurrency → errors/throttles → DLQ → logs → X-Ray → visibility.
Never scale before ruling out code errors and poison messages.
Pre-build CloudWatch dashboard with all runbook metrics.
60s: Age depth concurrency errors DLQ logs trace visibility. Fix root cause. Dashboard in alarm.
Follow-up: automate runbook steps with incident bot?
commonPitfalls: Blind concurrency increase on erroring Lambda — rejection answer.
Strong answer: Logs Insights first when Errors metric elevated.
Skipping DLQ inspection — poison message keeps retrying.
No pre-built dashboard — wastes incident minutes.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Adding messageId to every log line at receive time is ODD — makes runbook step 5 queryable; same discipline as correlation ID in ASP.NET middleware.
Runbook gaps become postmortem action items — same as Google's incident review timeline vs debug checklist.
